Question 2 integrated. Next:

**Question:** When the spec says a phone number is a `+` followed by 8 to 15 "decimal digits", should only the ordinary digits `0`-`9` count, or should digits from other writing systems (Arabic-Indic `٠١٢`, Devanagari, full-width `０１２`) count too? (FR-033, FR-034)

**Why it matters:** Log files picked up from real systems contain all sorts of text. If other writing systems' digits count, a line like `+٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨` gets redacted; if they don't, it passes through. The two readings also disagree about what `+12345678٩` is — whether that trailing foreign digit breaks the "followed by another digit" rule — so acceptance tests cannot be written until this is settled.

**Recommended:** Option A — the existing email, IPv4, and card rules are already defined and implemented over `0`-`9` only, so restricting phone to the same set keeps all four categories on one convention and keeps FR-052/FR-053's "nothing else changes" promise exact. The alternative silently widens recognition in a way the feature description never asked for.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Only `0`-`9` count, matching the existing email, IPv4, and card rules; a digit from another writing system neither forms part of a phone number nor triggers the followed-by-a-digit exclusion — it simply ends the candidate as any other character would |
| B | Any Unicode decimal digit counts, both toward the 8-to-15 length and toward the followed-by-a-digit exclusion |
| C | Only `0`-`9` form a phone number, but any Unicode decimal digit immediately after a candidate still excludes it (strictest reading — narrow recognition, wide exclusion) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
